name: Becher
title: Son of Benjamin
summary: Becher was one of the sons of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as part of the tribe of Benjamin, which later became one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Although little is known about his personal life, his place in the family record is important for understanding the tribal structure of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the sons of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Becher is listed as one of Benjamin's sons when Jacob's family went down to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's family in Egypt
keyEvents.description: Becher was part of the larger group of 70 people from Jacob's household who settled in Egypt during the famine.

keyEvents.title: The Genealogy in the Book of Numbers
keyEvents.description: In the census of the Book of Numbers, Benjamin's descendants are recorded, and Becher's lineage is mentioned as the family of the Becherites.

keyEvents.title: Becher's Descendants in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: 1 Chronicles gives a detailed list of Becher's sons and their families, which numbered 20,200 men fit for battle.

keyEvents.title: The Significance of the Tribe of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Benjamin, to which Becher belonged, became an important tribe in Israel's history and gave rise to figures such as King Saul and the apostle Paul.
